questions.q: How many total GPUs does the solara-train cluster have, and how are they arranged?
questions.explain: solara-train has 64 nodes with 8 NVIDIA H100 GPUs each, for 512 GPUs total — NVLink connects GPUs within a node, InfiniBand connects the nodes.

questions.q: Which interconnect links the 8 GPUs inside a single solara-train node to each other?
questions.explain: NVLink is the intra-node GPU-to-GPU interconnect, giving each H100 up to 900 GB/s of bidirectional bandwidth to its peers. InfiniBand connects nodes to each other, not GPUs within a node.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four core jobs the training infrastructure has to do, independent of the model being trained?
options: Keep the GPUs fed so the network isn't the bottleneck
Survive failures over the course of a long run
Choose the model's learning rate schedule
Checkpoint and resume progress after a crash
questions.explain: Choosing a learning rate schedule is an algorithm decision, not an infrastructure one. The infrastructure's jobs are feeding GPUs, surviving failures, checkpointing, and scheduling — covered in Lesson 3's infrastructure-vs-algorithms split.

questions.q: In the torchrun command shown in this lesson, what do --nnodes and --nproc_per_node describe?
options: Hyperparameters of the model being trained
The number of machines and the number of processes to launch per machine
The number of attention heads and layers in Solara-70B
questions.explain: --nnodes sets the total number of machines and --nproc_per_node sets how many processes (typically one per GPU) to launch on each — both are facts about the cluster, not the model.

questions.q: Which custom resource does the Kubeflow Training Operator use to launch a distributed PyTorch job on solara-train's Kubernetes cluster?
questions.explain: The Kubeflow Training Operator provides the PyTorchJob custom resource (CRD) specifically for orchestrating distributed PyTorch training jobs, built on top of standard Kubernetes Pods.
